# RuGraph scoped security review

Date: 2026-10-16. Scope: the two new Rust crates, SDKs, CLI, their boundaries,
and the additive GraphDB visitor API. Authorized work: implementation, local
read only scanning and correction of defects in the new implementation. No
production systems, external provider credentials or real user data were used.

## Trust model

| Boundary | Threat | Mitigation and residual responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Untrusted text/JSON → program | Type confusion, duplicate fields, excessive input | Strict parsing, version checks, one representation, hard size/depth bounds |
| Program → host authority | Self granted permissions or arbitrary effects | Host grants checked separately; only three effects; no general I/O operations |
| Snapshot → runtime | Dangling references, oversized properties, excessive derivation | Validation, work and result limits, bounded provenance, fixed point over admitted facts |
| GraphDB → snapshot | Allocation before checking; inconsistent concurrent reads | Borrowed bounded visitors; caller must exclude every writer |
| Predictor → language | Mislabelled scores, malformed output, excessive results | Typed isolation, finite/identity/count checks, native preflight; custom predictors are trusted code |
| Model file → native scorer | Invalid shape, nonfinite weights, forged claimed metrics | Strict artifact bounds and native validation; host trusts producer or reruns evaluation |
| SDK → local executable | Shell injection, output flood, indefinite process | Argument arrays, explicit paths, timeout and bounded pipe draining |
| Receipt → consumer | Tampering or treating a checksum as authenticity | Checksum verification and full replay; authentication is explicitly outside scope |

## Confirmed fixes and validation

The independent review confirmed oversized graph capture and native prediction
allocation paths. Both were fixed at the boundary before copying or accumulating
payloads. Regression tests and the repeated native memory reproducer pass.
JSON roundtrip, request validation, nested canonical hashing, Python output
draining, JavaScript numeric precision and CLI preflight defects were also fixed
and covered by executed tests. No unresolved high or critical finding remains
within this focused code review scope.

The SDK executable and model paths are trusted host configuration. The clients
are not OS sandboxes for arbitrary hostile binaries. A trusted custom Rust
Predictor can perform work outside the interpreter's accounting; only the
provided native implementation preflights its internal scoring work.

## Tools and coverage

Read only scans used the validated `@claude-flow/cli@3.25.6` runtime:

```bash
npx --yes @claude-flow/cli@3.25.6 security scan \
  --target crates/ruvector-language --depth deep --type all
npx --yes @claude-flow/cli@3.25.6 security scan \
  --target crates/ruvector-language-native --depth deep --type all
npx --yes @claude-flow/cli@3.25.6 security scan \
  --target python/ruvector-language --depth deep --type all
```

The npm package was copied into an isolated temporary directory, its empty
dependency lockfile generated with scripts disabled, and both `npm audit --json`
and the same Ruflo scan run from that directory. This avoids auditing the
monorepo parent's unrelated npm dependency tree. The SDK declares no runtime or
development dependencies; the isolated audit reported zero dependencies and zero
advisories. Scoped Ruflo scans reported no findings. Scanner output is supporting
evidence, not a proof of safety.

Scan date and npm advisory retrieval date: 2026-10-16. The service did not expose
an advisory database snapshot timestamp, so an exact feed revision is unknown.
The initial feature review did not include Cargo transitive advisory auditing.
A subsequent CI review identified an existing root dependency advisory gate
failure. The root rustls lock entry is updated to the patched 0.23.46 release,
with unchanged registry dependency requirements, features and minimum Rust
version. The downloaded archive checksum and compilation were verified.
The Graph language workflow now audits both standalone lockfiles with
`cargo-audit` 0.22.2; existing root jobs audit the root lockfile. Passing the
functional acceptance suite alone does not establish advisory clearance.
Python build tools and the host runtime are outside the zero runtime dependency
claim. Other root repository vulnerabilities are outside this feature review.

Rust lockfile hashes, compiler versions, full acceptance commands and results
are recorded in [ACCEPTANCE.md](ACCEPTANCE.md). No secret values are included in
this report or the committed fixtures.

## Counterfactual audit extension, 2026-10-16

Threat: a caller requests repeated evaluations or oversized reports, disguises
missing targets as robustness, supplies ambiguous JSON, or triggers model/provider
effects during an audit. Mitigations: 64 trial cap, aggregate worst-case execution
reservation capped at one billion, validated snapshots before copying, incremental
16 MiB report accounting, missing/duplicate target rejection, strict CLI JSON,
normal capability checks, and rejection of every prediction step. Audit overhead
outside the runtime meter is bounded structurally, not billed as runtime work.

SDK options are written into private temporary files and deleted on both success
and error. Tests check file permissions and cleanup, real process execution and
aggregate budget errors. Audit reports contain caller-supplied evidence identities
and must be handled with the same access policy as ordinary receipts.

Read-only Ruflo scan command: `npx -y @claude-flow/cli@3.25.6 security scan --target
crates/ruvector-language --depth deep --type all`. Completed with zero findings.
Manual boundary review and regression tests supplement scanner coverage. No new
dependencies or lockfile changes; this scan is not a refreshed advisory-feed audit
and does not prove absence of vulnerabilities. Source identity authenticity,
source independence and real-world causal interpretation remain outside scope.

## Prepared snapshots

The additive Rust API borrows an immutable snapshot; private cached fields cannot
be constructed or replaced by the caller. Safe Rust prevents mutation and use
after free while it exists. It retains no caller capabilities, clock, decisions
or model responses. Every execution rechecks program/context and provider calls.
Cached validation/index work is charged again, preserving low-budget rejection
and receipt accounting. Tests cover malformed snapshots, capability revocation,
invalid context, exhausted budgets and repeated provider invocation. No unsafe
code or new I/O boundary is introduced. Index memory is retained until the host
drops preparation; avoid retaining unbounded numbers of prepared snapshots.

## Exact selection and borrowed IDs

The optimizer changes only internal node ownership and physical sorting. It
introduces no unsafe code, dependency or external boundary. Every vector is still
validated before selection; malformed tail candidates cannot escape checks. Public
evidence, receipts and predictor requests remain owned. Borrowed IDs refer to the
immutable snapshot, not transient program strings. Historical logical work and
byte accounting are preserved. Full-sort oracle tests cover ties and extreme
finite values; real native and SDK boundaries remain in the acceptance gate.

# RuGraph version 1 specification

Package version: 0.1.0. Wire version: 1. Status: executable reference implementation.

## Purpose and architecture

RuGraph describes bounded graph computations whose outputs preserve the
distinction between observations, derived evidence and model predictions.
Readable source and strict JSON share one typed Program representation. Rust,
JavaScript, TypeScript and Python execute the same Rust runtime.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Text[Readable source] --> Check[Parse and type check]
  JSON[Strict JSON] --> Check
  Check --> Program[Versioned program]
  Program --> Run[Bounded runtime]
  Host[Snapshot and host grants] --> Run
  KGE[Native KGE adapter] --> Run
  Run --> Decisions[Evidence decisions]
  Run --> Predictions[Typed predictions]
  Decisions --> Receipt[Replay receipt]
  Predictions --> Receipt
```

The snapshot is immutable during one execution. The context supplies time and
capabilities. An embedded trusted predictor may perform model computation. The
core runtime has no ambient network, filesystem, shell, clock or provider access.

## Surface syntax

```text
program NAME {
  effect graph.read;
  effect model.predict;
  effect decision.emit;
  budget UNSIGNED_INTEGER;
  let NAME = OPERATION;
  ...
  emit NAME;
}
```

`//` comments end at newline. Strings use JSON quoting and escaping. Identifiers
match `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` and contain at most 128 bytes. Binding definitions
are ordered and unique. References must point to earlier bindings. A program
has one final emit. Effect declarations cannot repeat. The compiler rejects
unknown versions, fields, syntax, operators and type flows.

| Operation | Text arguments | Static result |
|---|---|---|
| nodes | `"label"` | Nodes |
| select | `["id", ...]` | Nodes |
| traverse | `binding "relation" depth integer` | Nodes |
| similar | `binding [finite_float, ...] top integer` | Nodes |
| observe | `binding "predicate" within integer` | Observations |
| infer | `[binding, ...] using ["rule_id", ...]` | Derived evidence |
| predict | `binding "relation" model "model_id" top integer` | Predictions |
| assess | `binding` | Decisions |

Traversal, similarity, observation and prediction consume nodes. Inference and
assessment consume observations or derived evidence. Only decisions or
predictions can be emitted. Programs declare `decision.emit`; graph operations
declare `graph.read`; prediction additionally declares `model.predict`.

JSON schema is the public Rust types in
[`types.rs`](../../../crates/ruvector-language/src/types.rs). JSON steps flatten
their operation, for example:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "name": "observe_service",
  "effects": ["graph.read", "decision.emit"],
  "budget": 100000,
  "steps": [
    {"bind": "n", "op": "select", "ids": ["api"]},
    {"bind": "e", "op": "observe", "input": "n", "predicate": "Failing", "within": 300},
    {"bind": "d", "op": "assess", "input": "e"}
  ],
  "emit": "d"
}
```

Duplicate keys, including nested or escaped duplicates, fail before typed
deserialization. Duplicate effects fail before set conversion. Generic JSON
input is at most 16 MiB with depth 64; programs are at most 1 MiB. The compiler
also enforces a 1 MiB serialized limit for Rust constructed programs.

## Graph semantics

Nodes have an ID, one label, JSON properties and an optional finite f32 vector.
Binary edges reference existing endpoints and have an ID and relation. Duplicate
record IDs and dangling edges are invalid. Selecting an unknown ID fails.

Traversal follows outgoing edges with the specified relation, includes the
seeds at distance zero, deduplicates nodes and terminates on cycles. Similarity
uses exact cosine ranking with stable ID tie breaks. It rejects a zero query or
dimension mismatch, and skips missing or zero candidate vectors. Exhaustive
ranking is bounded by work and result limits.

## Evidence and time

An observation has a signed boolean value, subject, predicate, source, unique ID,
observation time and expiry. It is live only when:

```text
observed_at <= now < expires_at
now - observed_at <= within
```

Freshness contributes an effective expiry of
`min(expires_at, observed_at + within + 1)`, with saturating integer arithmetic.
All timestamps and windows use one host chosen integer unit; examples use seconds.
The runtime never invents a wall clock value.

The evidence domain retains every selected subject and requested predicate even
when no observation matches. Assessment yields:

| Positive support | Negative support | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | No | supported |
| No | Yes | refuted |
| Yes | Yes | conflicting |
| No | No | unknown |

These statuses describe admitted evidence, not objective truth or probabilities.
A source identifier provides lineage; it does not authenticate or establish
independence of the source.

## Rules and retraction

Rules are finite conjunctions of explicitly signed predicates about the same
subject. Their conclusions are signed predicates. Inference computes a fixed
point over selected rules and input evidence; absence never satisfies a negative
premise. Unsupported cycles cannot create evidence.

Original observations remain distinct witnesses. A new supported signed fact
receives one deterministic canonical derivation, preserving the union of original
observation IDs, source IDs and rule IDs and the minimum expiry of its premises.
This does not enumerate every alternative proof. Input domains remain present
and selected rule conclusions add domains even when unsupported.

Each execution recomputes from its snapshot and clock. Deletion and expiry
therefore retract dependent conclusions without an incremental cache. Another
surviving witness can replace a deleted canonical witness on the next execution.

## Predictions and model lifecycle

The native adapter uses actual RuVector HolE or RotatE scoring over all entities
in a validated model vocabulary. A batch records model name, revision, artifact
hash, exact ranking flag, work and candidates. Prediction objects may refer to
entities outside the graph snapshot. They remain predictions and cannot become
evidence through inference or assessment.

Offline training uses the native Trainer, explicit split data, seed and bounded
configuration. Evaluation rejects train/evaluation overlap and unseen vocabulary.
Promotion is an explicit operation producing a new model bundle. Hashes and
metrics inside imported candidate files are not authenticated; the operator must
trust their producer or rerun the evaluation. No online self modification occurs.

## Execution authority and bounds

The program's declared effects must be a subset of host granted capabilities.
Execution charges deterministic units against
`min(program.budget, context.max_steps)`. These units account for validation,
indexing, scans, graph expansion, vector arithmetic, sorting, rule work,
provenance and native scoring. They are not milliseconds or exact CPU cycles.
Bounded parsing and static checking occur before runtime accounting.

| Boundary | Version 1 ceiling |
|---|---|
| Program operations | 1,024 |
| Vector dimensions | 4,096 |
| Traversal depth | 64 |
| Program list length or top k | 10,000 |
| Program or host work budget | 1,000,000,000 |
| Snapshot records combined | 100,000 |
| Snapshot serialized bytes | 16 MiB |
| Property nesting | 32 |
| Property values or rule premises | 100,000 each |
| Host result limit | 1 through 100,000 |
| Retained binding payload estimate | 16 MiB |

Result and provenance limits apply separately to collection sizes and reference
counts. Host configured result limits can be substantially lower than hard
ceilings. All error paths discard intermediate results. Bounds limit admitted
data and algorithmic work; they are not a formal memory safety or termination
proof for arbitrary host supplied Predictor code. Process clients additionally
apply timeout and output limits.

## Canonicalization and replay

Program struct field order and effect set order are fixed. Operation and program
array order are significant. Snapshot records are sorted by ID, rule premises
are sorted, and property object keys are recursively sorted; property arrays
retain order. This makes record insertion order and object key insertion order
irrelevant without claiming algebraic equivalence between distinct programs.

The receipt contains version, program/snapshot/context SHA256 hashes, snapshot
revision, logical time, work and typed output. Its checksum excludes the
`receipt_hash` field. Verification checks integrity only. Replay reexecutes and
requires complete receipt equality. Hashes are not signatures or evidence of
empirical truth. Pin the implementation and floating point environment for
archival reproducibility; cross platform FFT equality is not guaranteed.

## Deliberate exclusions

This version does not implement arbitrary graph mutation, tool calls, LLM
orchestration, probabilistic inference, automatic confidence calibration,
cross subject rule variables, incremental truth maintenance, distributed
execution, ANN planning, general purpose loops or a native code compiler.
It is a complete implementation of the bounded language specified here.

## Host counterfactual audit extension

The additive audit API does not add a language operation or change receipt wire
version 1. See [ADR-GL-006](../../adr/ADR-GL-006-bounded-counterfactual-audits.md)
for its separate version 1 report contract and [FRONTIER.md](FRONTIER.md) for CLI
and SDK examples. Audit is restricted to decision programs without prediction
steps. Each intervention is independent of the others.

## Prepared Rust host execution

`runtime::PreparedSnapshot` borrows a validated immutable snapshot and reuses its
indexes and canonical hash across queries. It changes actual preparation cost,
not language semantics or deterministic work. Every query uses fresh program,
context and optional provider calls. Complete receipts match ordinary execution.
This is not a process SDK cache or incremental graph update facility. See
[ADR-GL-007](../../adr/ADR-GL-007-immutable-prepared-snapshots.md).

# Portable execution and learning validation

Validated 2026-10-16 with Rust 1.90.0, wasm-bindgen 0.2.105, Node 24.19 and Python 3.12.14. Upstream RuVector revision: `f017d5f10c78b95843614f040f5cf22bfc1b3ac8`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Existing core, native, JavaScript and Python suites | 90 passed |
| Actual WASM runtime and installed npm package | 11 passed plus installation smoke |
| RVF wire format, boundaries and CLI | 7 passed |
| SONA learning, promotion guards and RVF integration | 5 passed |
| Native/WASM replay, audit and learning report in RVF | Passed |
| Real Chrome web module execution | Passed |
| Rust formatting and strict Clippy | Passed |
| Three new Cargo lockfile advisory audits | No advisories reported |
| Ruflo 3.25.6 scoped deep source scan | No findings reported |

The browser was exercised on the Software Factory desktop using the generated web module and the checked-in browser harness. Its receipt hash was `e4e90e445cc6f17d438baeefd42309656d7909572ca53a649fa9d1071b4b26cd`, matching the native fixture and the portable pipeline. The remote bundle lacked the native executable; native comparison was performed by the local parity and pipeline tests. CI runs both in one checkout.

The generated Node WASM module measured 851,226 bytes. The build limits linear memory to 256 MiB, with 16 MiB string boundaries. Host JavaScript allocations are additional. A host Worker is needed for termination deadlines.

An integrated test exposed floating point drift in JSON learning attachments. RVF now enables serde_json float_roundtrip; a deterministic attachment regression covers 999 floating point values, and the actual learning report round trip passes.

## Optimization evidence

The checked-in [raw report](../../../crates/ruvector-language-learning/reports/strategy-learning.json) measured 79.44% lower batch latency for the learned policy versus cold execution. Static prepared execution measured 79.46%. Training took approximately 231 ms. These measurements demonstrate the value of prepared execution on this synthetic workload; they do not demonstrate an advantage from learning over a static prepared policy. All receipts matched, both SONA MicroLoRA states changed, and no trajectories were dropped. Timings vary between runs, so CI does not require a timing win.

Learning is host advisory, promotion requires all held-out cases to clear a 10% gate, and rollback remains explicit. The serialized report is not a resumable model checkpoint. RVF verifies container and receipt integrity; it neither authenticates the producer nor grants execution authority. Request/receipt binding requires independent replay with trusted host context.

The source scan covered the three new Rust boundaries and the WASM JavaScript package, excluding generated files and build outputs. Automated scan results are limited evidence, supplemented by rejection tests for malformed input, resource bounds, authority and corruption. The new SVG was rendered and visually inspected.

## Reproduce

Follow the toolchain setup in [CONTRIBUTING](../../../CONTRIBUTING.md), then run:

```bash
bash scripts/test-graph-language.sh
bash scripts/test-graph-language-wasm.sh
bash scripts/test-graph-language-rvf.sh
bash scripts/test-graph-language-learning.sh
bash scripts/test-graph-language-portable.sh
python3 scripts/test-graph-language-browser.py
```

#!/usr/bin/env python3 """Exercise the actual web loader in local headless Chrome after the WASM build.""" from functools import partial from http.server import SimpleHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer from pathlib import Path import json import os import re import shutil import subprocess import threading root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] chrome = os.environ.get('CHROME_BIN') or next( (p for name in ('google-chrome', 'chromium', 'chromium-browser') if (p := shutil.which(name))), None) if not chrome: raise SystemExit('Chrome is required; set CHROME_BIN to its executable') class Quiet(SimpleHTTPRequestHandler): def log_message(self, *_args): pass server = ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), partial(Quiet, directory=str(root))) thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True) thread.start() try: url = f'http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_port}/npm/packages/graph-language-wasm/test/browser.html' result = subprocess.run( [chrome, '--headless', '--no-sandbox', '--disable-gpu', '--disable-dev-shm-usage', '--virtual-time-budget=10000', '--dump-dom', url], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=45, check=True) match = re.search(r'
PASS ([a-f0-9]{64})
', result.stdout) if not match: message = re.search(r'
(.*?)
', result.stdout, re.S) raise SystemExit(f'Browser smoke failed: {message.group(1) if message else result.stderr[-1500:]}') # Compare to the native executable when present, rather than asserting a hardcoded hash. binary = Path(os.environ.get('RUGRAPH_REFERENCE_BIN', str(root / 'crates/ruvector-language/target/debug/rvg-core'))) native_verified = binary.is_file() if native_verified: examples = root / 'crates/ruvector-language/examples' native = subprocess.check_output( [str(binary), 'run', str(examples/'incident.rvg'), '--snapshot', str(examples/'snapshot.json'), '--context', str(examples/'context.json')], text=True) assert json.loads(native)['receipt_hash'] == match.group(1), 'Browser/native receipt mismatch' print(json.dumps({'browser': 'PASS', 'receipt_hash': match.group(1), 'native_comparison': native_verified})) finally: server.shutdown() server.server_close() thread.join(timeout=5)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the full UI through the real module Worker and WASM in Chrome."""
from functools import partial
from http.server import SimpleHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from pathlib import Path
import html,json,os,re,shutil,subprocess,threading
root=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
chrome=os.environ.get('CHROME_BIN') or next((p for n in ('google-chrome','chromium','chromium-browser') if (p:=shutil.which(n))),None)
if not chrome: raise SystemExit('Chrome required; set CHROME_BIN')
class Quiet(SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self,*args):pass
server=ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1',0),partial(Quiet,directory=str(root)))
thread=threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever,daemon=True);thread.start()
try:
    result=subprocess.run(['node','--experimental-websocket',str(root/'scripts/explorer-chrome.mjs'),f'http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_port}/explorer/test/browser.html'],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=120)
    if result.returncode: raise SystemExit(result.stderr or result.stdout)
    print(result.stdout.strip())
finally:
    server.shutdown();server.server_close();thread.join(timeout=5)

# ADR-GL-004: Native RuVector adapters and explicit model lifecycle

**Status**: Implemented, validation recorded in the acceptance report
**Date**: 2026-10-16

## Decision

The native language package imports real ruvector-graph and ruvector-kge crates.
Graph capture requires the caller to hold its writer gate: GraphDB exposes
concurrent individual operations, not a language-level multi-object snapshot
transaction. The adapter's quiescence precondition is explicit. The language
snapshot supports one label per node and binary edges; unsupported graph data
is rejected rather than silently dropped.

The KGE provider uses RuVector Tables and HolE/RotatE scorers. It performs exact,
bounded exhaustive candidate ranking with deterministic tie order. Version 1
does not use ANN or assert calibrated probability. Predictions carry model name,
revision, content hash, exactness and charged work. Predictions may refer to an
entity in the model vocabulary that has no node in the snapshot; they remain
tagged predictions and cannot become observations or graph nodes implicitly.

Model artifacts are inert data. The offline model tool separates training,
evaluation and explicit promotion. Training creates a candidate, not a change
to a live registry. Split boundaries and measured metrics belong to the artifact
and report. Promotion is a host decision against declared acceptance conditions.
Randomly initialized weights are not described as learned or accurate.

The core binary is rvg-core and fails if a model provider is requested. The
native rvg binary supplies the real provider. Both share one parser, runtime and
CLI. TypeScript and Python clients launch the selected executable with argument
arrays and shell disabled. They perform no installation or network activity.

## Alternatives

Embedding Python or JavaScript evaluation into the runtime would widen the
authority boundary and duplicate evidence semantics. Direct native bindings
could reduce process startup cost but add build and ABI complexity. Process
bindings are selected for the initial version and their overhead is reported
separately from in-process execution.

## Acceptance

Native tests compare scorer output with direct RuVector APIs, capture a real
GraphDB and execute a language program against it, reject incompatible model
shapes and unsupported graph content, and exercise the offline model lifecycle.
These validate software contracts, not accuracy on a customer dataset. Published
KGE quality or cross-graph generalization requires separate held-out experiments.

# ADR-GL-013: Local WASM tutorial and graph explorer

Status: Accepted

## Context

RuGraph needs an accessible way to demonstrate graph programs and inspect evidence without installing a compiler or granting a service access to user input. The RuVector Explorer establishes the visual language: dark graph canvas, compact instruments, mint, orange and blue accents.

## Decision

Publish a buildless HTML, CSS and ES module application on GitHub Pages, built from this repository. Compile the existing pinned Rust WASM crate during CI and copy only the web bindings, wrapper and runtime into the distribution. `build.json` records the source revision and asset SHA256 hashes. Generated output remains untracked.

Six lessons cover graph traversal, contradiction, expiry, capability rejection, exact cosine candidate retrieval, and independent counterfactual audits. Programs, snapshots and host context remain editable. The UI preserves raw JSON across the Worker boundary so Rust performs strict duplicate-key and integer validation. Display parsing does not feed execution. After custom JSON edits, scenario controls are disabled until lesson restore to prevent lossy JSON rewriting.

Run each operation in a dedicated module Worker, with a single outstanding request, a 15 second initialization deadline and an 8 second execution deadline. Terminate and replace the Worker after timeout or explicit reset. The Rust build caps linear memory at 256 MiB; JavaScript allocations are additional. The public editors are limited to 1 MiB each. Display at most 200 nodes, 500 edges and 100 decision cards while retaining the full raw receipt for explicit export. The host latency measurement includes compilation, message transfer and runtime execution; it is not a benchmark of Rust alone.

All output uses text nodes. The content security policy restricts scripts, Workers and fetches to the same origin, with WASM compilation enabled. No analytics, third-party scripts, external fonts, persistence or runtime API calls are required. Source links navigate only when selected. The SVG graph is an illustrative dependency layout; evidence statuses come from actual receipts. Motion respects reduced-motion preferences and can be paused. Keyboard node selection and a searchable button list offer alternatives to the graph. Phones use a separate portrait coordinate layout with at least 44 px node hit areas, a native lesson picker and a persistent Run dock. Curved paths, orbital rings and a scanning beam animate through CSS without a frame loop. Motion can be paused globally, including the header and atmosphere; reduced motion disables scene animation. A CSS immersive mode provides an exit-capable fallback when the Fullscreen API is absent.

Deploy only after lesson contracts, Worker cancellation/recovery tests and actual Chrome UI acceptance pass. Pull requests build and test without deploying. A deployment rollback is a revert followed by the same workflow, or redeployment of the previous successful artifact.

## Alternatives

A server evaluator adds hosting cost and a data trust boundary without improving this tutorial. A second JavaScript interpreter risks divergent evidence semantics. A WebGL dependency increases initial size and compatibility cost for a twelve-node teaching graph. GitHub Pages keeps source, builds and public demo together and follows the existing RuVector deployment convention.

## Consequences and acceptance

The demo offers portable core behavior. SONA remains a native host experiment; RVF remains a data container. Neither is simulated as browser learning or trusted execution.

`node --test explorer/test/lessons.test.mjs` verifies real WASM lesson results, strict JSON, replay and Worker lifecycle. After `bash scripts/build-explorer.sh`, `python3 scripts/test-explorer-browser.py` checks the actual tutorial controls, edits, permissions, expiry, audits, mobile overflow and reset through the browser Worker.

# RuGraph research and acceptance frontier

Reviewed 2026-10-16. Goal: auditable agent memory decisions with reproducible
failure analysis. This is engineering informed by current research, not a claim
that RuGraph is state of the art across graph programming or AI reasoning.

## Research to implementation

| Primary source | Established direction | RuGraph action | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Souffle provenance](https://souffle-lang.github.io/provenance) | Proof explanation is mature prior art | Preserve explicit witness lineage; distinguish witness replacement from changed truth status | No minimal proof tree or all proof enumeration |
| [Why Neighborhoods Matter, May 2026 preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.15109) | Ablations can expose dependence on graph context beyond final citations | Add edge, observation and source ablation with full recomputation | No full traversal trace or graph node masking |
| [GraphRAG-Bench](https://graphrag-bench.github.io/) | Evaluate graph retrieval and reasoning across task types | Independent application oracle, generated variations, raw samples | No public corpus QA benchmark or comparison against external systems |

## Runnable agent memory application

From the RuVector root, with Rust 1.90:

```bash
cargo run --release --locked --manifest-path crates/ruvector-language/Cargo.toml --example agent_memory
cargo run --release --locked --manifest-path crates/ruvector-language/Cargo.toml --example agent_memory -- request > memory-request.json
cargo run --release --locked --manifest-path crates/ruvector-language/Cargo.toml --example agent_memory_bench
```

The application ranks synthetic memory vectors, traverses related memories,
checks recent signed reliability observations, derives usability using positive
and negative rules, and audits the effect of removing either source or one edge.
It asserts decision equivalence with a direct evaluator before emitting results.
There is no LLM, API charge, model download, learned embedding quality claim or
personal information in the fixture. The vectors and source identities are synthetic.

## Counterfactual audit API

Rust: `ruvector_language::audit::run(&request, &options)`.
JavaScript: `await client.audit(request, options)`.
Python: `client.audit(request, options)`.
Both core and native CLIs accept:

```bash
rvg-core audit --request request.json --audit-options options.json
```

Example options for the bundled incident fixture:

```json
{
  "interventions": [
    {"kind": "observation", "id": "db-error-1"},
    {"kind": "source", "id": "telemetry-a"},
    {"kind": "edge", "id": "api-db"}
  ],
  "max_execution_work": 400000
}
```

`changes` lists only status/domain changes; `changed_decisions` also counts
witness changes. A null before/after means the subject/predicate is not in that
execution's decision domain. Unknown means it was assessed with neither sign.
A no-change result does not prove a source is irrelevant in other contexts or
joint interventions. Compare full audit reports to reproduce an audit; the
ordinary receipt `verify` command does not accept audit reports.

## Benchmark contract

The status-only handwritten baseline and RuGraph see identical graph, vectors,
observations and time. Their statuses must match. The baseline omits validation,
capability checks, resource budgets, provenance and hashing, so timing ratios
are feature-cost comparisons, not an equivalent-feature speed contest. Neither
path includes parsing, SDK startup or storage capture. The audit timing includes
one baseline and three full executions. Raw sorted samples and environment are
in [agent-memory-benchmark.json](agent-memory-benchmark.json). Reproduce on the
deployment host; shared container timings are noisy. RSS is not measured by this
harness. No code-reduction percentage is claimed.

## Acceptance trace

| Requirement | Executable evidence |
|---|---|
| Source sensitivity and redundant evidence | `tests/audit.rs` necessary/redundant/conflict cases |
| Graph context effects | edge deletion distinguishes absent domain from unknown |
| Independent decision semantics | 256 generated cases plus 64 oracle ablations |
| Canonical receipts | input reversal and repeated audit equality |
| Resource and authority bounds | invalid targets, trial caps, reservation limits, capability denial, prediction rejection |
| Process integration | CLI audit and JS/Python real binary tests |
| Private temporary files | SDK permission and cleanup tests on both paths |
| Performance transparency | three sizes, 5 warmups, 30 samples, raw data |

Next research gate: evaluate a real application dataset and compare an equivalent
handwritten implementation with the same governance features. Until then, retain
preview positioning. External benchmark leadership and research novelty remain
unestablished.

## Reuse without stale decisions

The new Rust `PreparedSnapshot` API reuses validation, indexes and the canonical
snapshot hash under an immutable borrow. It recomputes decisions with a fresh
context and preserves complete receipts and logical budgets. See
[ADR-GL-007](../../adr/ADR-GL-007-immutable-prepared-snapshots.md) and the
[paired measurements](prepared-specialized-benchmark.json). This addresses repeated
host-query cost; it is not an incremental engine or a cache of authority/model
outputs. The cold path and process SDK behavior remain semantically unchanged.

A rejected hash buffer experiment and first prepared candidate are retained with
the final results to make selection visible. Warm improvements do not establish
cold-path improvements, production service latency or superiority over other
languages. A dedicated-host performance run and real dataset remain the next
external validation gates.

## Exact selection and allocation reduction

Exact cosine ranking now partitions candidates and sorts only the top K. Runtime
node sets borrow immutable node IDs; owned data remains at public output/provider
boundaries. The logical work and retained-byte charges remain unchanged to preserve
receipts and limits. The paired two-dimensional fixture measured an additional
10.73% to 42.57% reduction in prepared latency. This does not predict performance
for high-dimensional embeddings or large K. See [raw paired evidence](selection-borrowing-benchmark.json)
and [ADR-GL-008](../../adr/ADR-GL-008-exact-selection-and-borrowed-node-sets.md).

# RuGraph v0.1 acceptance evidence

Validated on 2026-10-16 against repository base
`46d816ddc4c2a8a06cd3613534a79b1d557d858b`.
This report covers the version 1 bounded language in [SPEC.md](SPEC.md).

## Result

Local acceptance passed: **90 tests**, formatting, strict targeted Clippy, ADR
number validation, packed npm client execution with TypeScript declarations,
and installed Python wheel execution and replay. No tests were skipped.

The implementation includes the text and JSON frontends, type/effect checks,
deterministic runtime, evidence and rule semantics, replay receipts, real
RuVector graph/KGE adapters, offline model lifecycle, CLI, process SDKs,
examples, eight ADRs and a scoped CI workflow. Package publication and default
branch merge are separate release actions.

## Reproduction

Install Rust 1.90.0 with rustfmt and Clippy, Node.js 24, Python 3.12, setuptools
and wheel. The package smoke script downloads TypeScript 5.9.3 through npm;
it does not publish a package. Run from the repository root:

```bash
bash scripts/test-graph-language.sh
bash scripts/smoke-graph-language-packages.sh
cargo +1.90.0 run --release --locked \
  --manifest-path crates/ruvector-language-native/Cargo.toml --example native_bench
```

The two acceptance scripts completed with exit code 0. Exact local versions:
rustc 1.90.0 (`1159e78c4`, 2025-09-14), Node.js 24.19.0, Python 3.12.14,
setuptools 84.0.0, wheel 0.48.0. Target: Linux x86_64, glibc 2.39.
The checked in workflow uses the same Rust, Python and Node major versions.
The dedicated remote acceptance workflow also passed at commit
`01d961f2d48528b3cf320d335adefa0f1245dc79`:
[Graph language run 38899871818](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/actions/runs/38899871818).
Broader repository checks are separate from that successful feature gate.

| Four evidence states; explicit negative support; temporal freshness | `tests/runtime.rs`, part of 15 tests | Pass |
| Signed conjunction, chained derivation, source lineage, cycles | `tests/runtime.rs` | Pass |

## Independent review and regressions

The compiler, runtime and native implementation were built in separate work
streams, then cross reviewed against the shared specification. Integration and
review found and fixed:

1. Flattened operation deserialization incorrectly rejected valid JSON fields.
   Canonical JSON and combined request roundtrips now pass while unknown fields
   and duplicate effects remain rejected.
2. Nested property key order affected hashing when an embedding host enabled
   serde's insertion ordered map feature. Borrowed canonical serialization now
   sorts nested object keys and charges sorting work.
3. Graph capture cloned arbitrary payloads before validation. Borrowed fallible
   visitors now validate identities, depth and property bounds before copying.
4. Native prediction copied large candidate strings before the output limit.
   It now ranks score/index pairs and preflights output bytes before allocation.
5. Python buffered unbounded child output and JavaScript could round u64 values.
   Streaming limits and explicit numeric precision checks now fail closed.
6. Missing replay arguments were detected after request execution. Required
   flags are now checked before input or model loading.

For the native output regression, the identical 1,000 entity / 50 subject /
top 1,000 request with 512 byte identities fell from 90,312 KiB to 9,216 KiB
peak child RSS and returned `LIMIT` before candidate allocation. It is a
targeted synthetic regression, not a general memory usage guarantee.

## Performance evidence

Full machine, source hash, workload, measurements and previous runs are in
[native-benchmark.json](native-benchmark.json). The final run uses HolE,
32 dimensions, 256 entities, 8 subjects, top 5, five warmups and 30 samples.
Direct and adapter paths both rank score/index pairs and clone only top k.
Candidate scores and rankings match before timing starts.

| Path | Median µs | p95 µs |
|---|---:|---:|
| Direct native KGE | 406.690 | 580.892 |
| Native adapter | 418.458 | 1,520.381 |
| Full language runtime | 437.987 | 1,000.401 |

Observed median runtime overhead is **7.70%** for this workload. The shared build
environment showed substantial tail variance. The direct baseline omits
validation, permission checks and receipt hashing, so this does not establish
the proposed 10% equivalent work product gate. The proposed 30% application code
reduction has not been established. Both remain product evaluation targets.
Synthetic initialized weights measure execution only; toy training tests do not
establish useful real world prediction accuracy or transfer to unseen graphs.

## Dependency identity and review scope

| Lockfile | SHA256 |
|---|---|
| Core `Cargo.lock` | `2381cce2e1ec9e372714914533e335bb6ec6866a96e17c2a2ad85e51e7f8dbe0` |
| Native `Cargo.lock` | `3beba443fc7ade7b251411c4e471f5728eb270b0cf7bfb578751de36d227fe5c` |

Both lockfiles are committed. A followup CI repair changes only the root
`rustls` lock entry from 0.23.45 to 0.23.46 and its registry checksum. Cargo
downloaded and verified the patched archive; dependency requirements, features
and minimum Rust version are identical in the registry records. The patched
library compiled with the root ring/std/tls12/logging feature profile in an
isolated Cargo check. Dedicated advisory checks now cover both standalone
language lockfiles; root advisory and lockfile integrity jobs validate the root
repair in CI. This does not suppress advisory findings. The
existing graph crate receives two additive borrowed visitor methods; existing
APIs keep their behavior. [SECURITY-REVIEW.md](SECURITY-REVIEW.md) records the
threat boundary, scanner scope, fixed findings and advisory coverage limits.

## Remaining limits

Graph capture requires caller enforced exclusion of all writers. The snapshot
profile supports one label per node, binary edges and no edge properties or
hyperedges. Predictions are transductive scorer outputs, not probabilities.
Imported model metrics and observation sources require host trust. Receipts
provide checksums, not signatures. Cross platform FFT bit equality is not
guaranteed. JavaScript accepts only safe integers; Python and Rust support u64.

No claim is made that all unrelated RuVector crates pass, that every transitive
dependency is vulnerability free, or that performance and accuracy targets have
been met outside the measured workload. This release implements the specified
bounded language; broader research extensions remain separate work.

## Immutable preparation followup

PreparedSnapshot is an additive Rust host API for repeated queries over a borrowed
immutable snapshot. Four new tests add 96 cold/warm query and clock comparisons,
invalid snapshot checks, capability revocation, budget equivalence and fresh
provider invocation. Complete receipts are equal, not only decision statuses.

Measured medians in microseconds, three alternating binary pairs, 30 samples per
path per pair, five warmups. The cold and prepared columns use the new binary;
preparation is measured independently:

| Nodes | Cold execution | Prepared execution | Preparation cost | Warm reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| 1024 | 3226.86 | 272.81 | 2840.60 | 91.55% |
| 4096 | 13078.38 | 930.38 | 12181.73 | 92.89% |

These are warm query reductions on synthetic fixtures, excluding initial
preparation. Median estimates suggest amortization within two queries; do not
interpret that estimate as a guarantee. The retained indexes consume memory until
dropped; resident memory was not measured. No changes to process SDK caching or

Cold old/new differences range from a 2.59% reduction to a 3.52% increase; audit
differences range from a 2.60% reduction to an 8.14% increase. The unchanged direct
control slowed 3.26% to 6.01%. This host does not establish zero regression or a

# Portable execution and governed learning

## Outcome

Run the same bounded RuGraph program in a browser or Node without spawning a
native process. Preserve requests, receipts, and learning reports in a portable
RVF capsule. Use actual RuVector SONA learning to propose host execution policies,
then evaluate the proposal before selecting it.

The business target is lower deployment friction and lower repeated query cost
while preserving the ability to explain and reproduce every evidence decision.
No improvement in application accuracy is implied by changing an execution policy.

## Contracts

| Requirement | Invariant | Acceptance evidence |
|---|---|---|
| WASM execution | Same program, snapshot and context retain core semantics | Native versus WASM receipt comparison; permissions, expiry, replay and audit tests |
| Portable artifacts | RVF contains bounded data with validated hashes | Upstream RVF wire roundtrip; corruption, truncation, duplicate and size rejection |
| Host authority | Artifact content never grants execution permissions | Capsule verification does not execute programs or load executable segments |
| Learning | Actual SONA consumes bounded execution trajectories | Learned state changes and pattern retrieval are recorded |
| Promotion | Candidate must pass a frozen evaluation | At least 10% measured benefit and zero receipt differences on held out workloads |
| Rollback | Baseline remains available | Rejected or unsuitable candidates retain the ordinary execution strategy |
| Honest cost | Preparation belongs to the candidate's cost | Compare complete batches, including snapshot preparation, using paired timings |
| Data separation | Evaluation data does not train the proposer | Disjoint workload identifiers and distinct synthetic evaluation cases |

## Control flow

1. Parse and validate the program, immutable snapshot and host context.
2. Execute through the native or WASM core, preserving the normal work charges.
3. Measure bounded training batches under explicitly allowed host strategies.
4. Feed training trajectories to SONA. Treat its learned pattern as a proposal.
5. Freeze the candidate. Measure it on separate evaluation workloads and compare
   every result with ordinary execution. Include preparation in the candidate cost.
6. Reject nonfinite metrics, contamination, changed receipts and insufficient gains.
7. Retain the baseline for rollback. Store the report as data in an RVF capsule
   alongside a request and receipt, with no implied source authentication.

On a malformed capsule, return an error before interpreting its contents. On a
failed optimization gate, keep the baseline. Learning cannot rewrite the program,
its evidence, capabilities, resource limits, or the promotion checks.

## Architecture and scope

The deterministic language core stays independent of SONA and RVF. WASM is an
adapter to that core. RVF is a data transport boundary. Learning is a native host
activity that proposes strategies outside program evaluation. This separation
prevents adaptive state from silently changing a replayed decision.

WASM is not automatically faster than native Rust. Its deployment benefit is
running locally without a native subprocess. String transfer and JSON parsing
still cost time and allocations. Browser hosts should use a Worker when executing
untrusted or long running requests so the host can terminate work independently.

The optimization experiment compares ordinary execution with prepared immutable
snapshots. A static always prepared policy is an important alternative. Showing
that prepared execution beats cold execution does not prove that SONA beats that
static policy, generalizes to production, or improves model accuracy. SONA's
learned patterns are proposals; the frozen evaluator determines acceptance.

RVF integrity checks detect inconsistent or corrupted contents. A party able to
rewrite the data and recompute checksums can produce a new valid capsule. Source
authentication requires a separate trusted signature policy. This integration
never treats a capsule as authorization to execute its contents.

## Upstream sources

All RuVector integration dependencies use commit
`f017d5f10c78b95843614f040f5cf22bfc1b3ac8`.

* [SONA engine and learning components](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/tree/f017d5f10c78b95843614f040f5cf22bfc1b3ac8/crates/sona)
* [Darwin candidate and contamination guards](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/f017d5f10c78b95843614f040f5cf22bfc1b3ac8/crates/sona/src/darwin_guard.rs)
* [RVF wire and segment types](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/tree/f017d5f10c78b95843614f040f5cf22bfc1b3ac8/crates/rvf)
* [WebAssembly security model](https://webassembly.org/docs/security/)
* [WebAssembly host imports and portability](https://webassembly.org/docs/portability/)
* [wasm-bindgen string boundary](https://wasm-bindgen.github.io/wasm-bindgen/reference/types/str.html)

Implementation ADRs and executable scripts are the detailed contracts. Measured
results must identify the workload, environment, artifact revisions, timing scope,
and any rejected candidates. No general self improvement or research novelty claim
follows from these integrations.

    paths: ['explorer/**', 'npm/packages/graph-language-wasm/**', 'crates/ruvector-language/**', 'crates/ruvector-language-wasm/**', 'scripts/build-explorer.sh', 'scripts/test-explorer-browser.py', 'scripts/explorer-chrome.mjs', '.github/workflows/explorer.yml']
  pull_request:
    paths: ['explorer/**', 'npm/packages/graph-language-wasm/**', 'crates/ruvector-language/**', 'crates/ruvector-language-wasm/**', 'scripts/build-explorer.sh', 'scripts/test-explorer-browser.py', 'scripts/explorer-chrome.mjs', '.github/workflows/explorer.yml']
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: explorer-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
      - name: Install WASM toolchain
        run: |
          rustup toolchain install 1.90.0 --profile minimal
          rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown --toolchain 1.90.0
          cargo +1.90.0 install wasm-bindgen-cli --version 0.2.105 --locked
      - name: Build explorer and exact WASM package
        run: |
          bash scripts/build-explorer.sh
          wasm-bindgen crates/ruvector-language-wasm/target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/ruvector_language_wasm.wasm --target nodejs --out-dir npm/packages/graph-language-wasm/generated/node --out-name runtime
          echo '{"type":"commonjs"}' > npm/packages/graph-language-wasm/generated/node/package.json
      - name: Tutorial contracts and worker recovery
        run: node --test explorer/test/*.test.mjs
      - name: Real browser UI and mobile acceptance
        run: python3 scripts/test-explorer-browser.py
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: explorer/dist
  deploy:
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy explorer
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

# ADR-GL-005: Replay receipts and reproducible delivery gates

**Status**: Implemented, validation recorded in the acceptance report
**Date**: 2026-10-16

## Decision

Every successful execution produces a structured receipt containing hashes of
the program, full snapshot and context, explicit clock, work count and typed
output. Prediction output additionally identifies its model. The receipt hash
excludes its own hash field. Hashes detect changed bytes under the documented
canonicalization; they are not signatures, authentication or proof of truth.

The verify CLI checks receipt integrity only. Replay reexecutes the request
using the selected native model state, verifies the supplied receipt, and
requires full receipt equality. A changed clock, grant, snapshot, program or
model participating in the emitted predictions therefore invalidates replay.
Unused model bundles are not receipt inputs. Reusing an old revision string
cannot hide changed content. Program and property array ordering remain
significant; snapshot records and rule premises are canonically sorted.

CI runs locked core and native builds, unit/integration/adversarial tests, both
process SDK suites, packaged-client smoke tests, formatting and targeted lint.
Fixtures are synthetic and labelled accordingly. The benchmark records workload,
machine and sample counts. A measured result must never be substituted with a
target, source comment or provider success message.

## Proposed product gates

The research proposal suggested at least 30% less application code and no more
than 10% overhead relative to equivalent handwritten implementations. These are
product hypotheses, not automatically satisfied release claims. Comparing a
validated, hashed interpreter with an unchecked loop is a diagnostic, not an
equivalent-work speed contest. Report the distinction and optimize only after
correctness is established.

## Rollout and rollback

Deliver additive source, examples, docs, CI and a reviewable PR. Existing APIs
remain available. Package publication, default-branch merge and deployment are
separate release decisions. A user can install the native command from a pinned
checkout and roll back by replacing that binary and its model registry with the
previous versions. Immutable model artifacts support that rollback.

## Acceptance trace

The final trace lives in docs/research/graph-language/ACCEPTANCE.md and maps each
in-scope requirement to executed evidence. Missing gates must be named; a passing
targeted suite does not imply all unrelated repository crates pass.
